In-house markerless multi-camera body capture · camera A001

Where The Hundred Millimetres Goes

Four things on one frame, each changing exactly one part of the pipeline. Blue is what the cameras triangulated. Violet is that same capture driving a parametric body. Green is our rig scaled to the performer. Orange is the fixed character we ship. The capture was never the problem.

frame 000 / 149

Median agreement with the reference solve, same joints, same frames:

our raw capture36.1 · 41.3 mm
our capture → SMPL-X27.7 · 40.1 mm
our rig, sized to performer136.6 · 113.0 mm
our rig, as delivered151.6 · 137.8 mm

Our front end already reaches the reference. Driving a parametric body with our own capture lands at 27.7 mm — on performer 0, better than our own raw triangulation, because a body model pulls noisy points toward a shape a human can actually have. Against our own capture it sits at 11–15 mm, so it is following our data, not drifting to the reference.

The rig loses ~100 mm of that. Not the detector, not the fit, not the head or feet work. A 540 mm shoulder span driving performers who measure 346 and 363 — and 540 is outside the parametric body’s entire shape range, which reaches only 367.

An overfit caught on the way, and worth recording. The first shape fit reported 0.1 mm mean error and looked like a clean win. It was ten free shape parameters against eleven limb targets — it hit every target exactly and built a body with the head 624 mm below the pelvis. It only surfaced because the pose fit then blew up to 429–807 mm at the neck while every limb sat at 5–30. Fixed with the model’s own standardised-shape prior. A sub-millimetre fit on the terms you constrained is not evidence the answer is right — it is evidence you had enough parameters.

Instrument, not delivery

Nothing shipped changes. Both the parametric body and the reference solve are research-licensed and neither enters the delivery path — the run report declares them false and that stays true. And agreement with a reference is not accuracy: neither side has ground truth, so a change that improves agreement could be moving toward the reference’s own error. It is the best comparison available, one part at a time.

What this view is blind to

Depth. Both skeletons are projected into one camera, so a joint can sit perfectly on the image and still be wrong along the viewing ray — a convincing overlay is evidence of placement and never of accuracy. It is shown here because it answers a placement question honestly, not because it settles accuracy.
